US stocks fell on Tuesday as tech stocks sold off and elevated oil prices and government bond yields weighed on markets.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( [^IXIC](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EIXIC/)) fell 1.3%, leading the major indexes lower. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( [^DJI](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EDJI/)) declined by 0.2%, while the S&P 500 ( [^GSPC](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EGSPC/)) pulled back by 0.6%, extending losses after [a downbeat start to the trading week.](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-monday-august-17-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-oil-treasurys-094421171.html)

7,707.98 +16.22 (+0.21%)

At close: August 19 at 4:38:31 PM EDT

^GSPC^DJI ^IXIC

Oil prices climbed to their highest level in over two weeks after President Trump said he intends to inflict more economic pain on Iran and [threatened to "bomb" Oman](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/well-bomb-the-s-out-of-them-trump-threatens-oman-as-it-reportedly-moves-toward-a-deal-with-iran-155621451.html) if it interferes with the US's plans for the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude ( [BZ=F](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BZ=F/)) futures, the international benchmark, traded near $91 per barrel, and US benchmark West Texas Intermediate crude futures ( [CL=F](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CL=F/)) rose to $84 per barrel as the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve plunged to its [lowest level since 1982](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/article/the-strategic-petroleum-reserve-hasnt-been-this-low-since-reagan-was-filling-it-in-1982-critics-wonder-how-low-is-too-low-180740733.html).

Rising oil, [an AI borrowing spree](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/ai-driving-treasury-yields-just-093000747.html?.tsrc=372&ncid=crm_-2240951-20260817-0--A&bt_user_id_proof=MYmKMtbFxMgc3XAqiUPZn33g1jr6OV2xnexP285aBXsSw1VyJkYotJmm3SffjYrrKaRDUhgvmsyD2O3a1twjSTenUJjfJjRupbWoA4Ad%2Feb6NbGeLUvzvsdQHtCVhdNL&bt_ts_proof=1787005901660), and concerns over government borrowing have also lifted bond yields globally in recent days. The 10-year Treasury yield ( [^TNX](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5ETNX/)) eased somewhat but remained elevated at 4.70%, and the 30-year yield ( [^TYX](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5ETYX/)) held near a 19-year high.

Earnings, meanwhile, have supported equities so far this reporting season. While the second quarter reporting period has slowed, Home Depot's ( [HD](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/HD/)) stock was little changed after reporting an improvement in sales for the second quarter as customers leaned toward smaller projects over the summer, and Klarna ( [KLAR](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/KLAR/)) [stock plunged on a trimmed outlook.](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/klarna-stock-plunges-20-on-trimmed-guidance-as-german-retail-sales-slow-141517463.html)

The [S&P 500](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.SPX/) and [Nasdaq Composite](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.IXIC/) dipped on Wednesday, pressured by a broad decline in tech. Investors also weighed mixed retail earnings results and the Federal Reserve's latest meeting minutes release.

The broad market index slipped 0.24% to close at 6,395.78, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq lost 0.67% and settled at 21,172.86. Wednesday marked a fourth day of losses for the S&P 500 and a second negative session for the Nasdaq. The [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.DJI/) was the outlier, adding 16.04 points, or 0.04%, and settling at 44,938.31.

Investors continued to take profits from several heavyweight technology and semiconductor names, fanning concerns about their high valuations and the strength of the artificial intelligence trade longer term. [Nvidia](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/NVDA/) ended the session marginally lower, while [Advanced Micro Devices](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/AMD/) and [Broadcom](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/AVGO/) each lost around 1%. Shares of [Palantir](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/PLTR/) declined about 1%, and [Intel](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/INTC/) dropped about 7%. Mega-cap tech companies [Apple](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/AAPL/), [Amazon](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/AMZN/), [Alphabet](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/GOOGL/) and [Meta Platforms](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/META/) also declined.

"It's not a surprise to see some investors taking profits in tech stocks, which have had an incredibly strong run – with some up over 80% since the early April lows. Market volume in general is typically quite sparse in late August leading to wider swings than fundamentals would warrant," said Carol Schleif, chief market strategist at BMO Private Wealth.

On the earnings front,[Target](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/TGT/) shares dropped 6% after the retailer [reported another decline in sales](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/08/20/target-tgt-q2-2025-earnings.html) and announced a new CEO who will step into the role on Feb. 1. [Lowe's](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/LOW/), meanwhile, edged higher after the home improvement retailer's [earnings beat expectations](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/08/20/lowes-low-q2-2025-earnings.html).

Minutes from the Federal Reserve's July meeting released Wednesday [showed that central bankers expressed concerns](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/08/20/fed-minutes-august-2025.html) about the state of the labor market and inflation, though most agreed that it was too soon to lower interest rates. At the time, policymakers once more held steady on interest rates, but Fed Governors Christopher Waller and Michelle Bowman [dissented](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/08/01/fed-governors-bowman-waller-explain-their-dissents-say-waiting-to-cut-rates-threatens-economy.html), marking the first time two voting Fed officials have done so since 1993.

"Participants generally pointed to risks to both sides of the Committee's dual mandate, emphasizing upside risk to inflation and downside risk to employment," the minutes noted. While "a majority of participants judged the upside risk to inflation as the greater of these two risks" a couple saw "downside risk to employment the more salient risk."

The release of the minutes come ahead of remarks from Fed Chair Jerome Powell on Friday, which investors will monitor for insights into the path of interest rates. Fed funds futures are pricing in a more than 80% likelihood of the central bank cutting interest rates at its next policy gathering in September, according to CME's [FedWatch tool.](https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html)

"If Powell's language is more hawkish, that could pressure tech stocks even further, as a continuation of these elevated interest rates is generally a headwind for the tech sector," Schleif said.

## Morgan Stanley warns UnitedHealth may be a "prolonged turnaround story"

Sopa Images \| Lightrocket \| Getty Images

[News](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/08/15/unitedhealth-shares-soar-after-warren-buffetts-new-stake-provides-a-vote-of-confidence.html) last week that famed investors including [Berkshire Hathaway](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/BRK.B/)'s [Warren Buffett](https://www.cnbc.com/warren-buffett/) are scooping up shares of [UnitedHealth](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/UNH/) have given the health insurer quite the boost. Shares have surged more than 11% over the past week, but remain down 40% year to date.

Despite the increased investor interest, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright is trimming back her UnitedHealth estimates and price target.

"We are lowering our estimates & Price Target to reflect a more prolonged turnaround story post 2Q revelations," Wright told clients in a reseach note. She said there is the potential for UnitedHealth to top estimates as its recovery plays out. However, she is making "more conservative assumptions at this juncture."

Among the signals Wright is looking for are some proof that the company's Medicare Advantage and its Optum Health businesses can improve their margins.

Wright's new price target is $325, down from $342, and suggests shares could rise 12% from Tuesday's close.

_—Christina Cheddar Berk_

## Bank of America downgrades Novavax

Shares of [Novavax](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/NVAX/) shed about 7.5% following a downgrade at Bank of America to underperform from neutral Wednesday. The bank also cut its price target to $7 from $9, implying 5% downside from Tuesday's close.

Analyst Alec Stranahan cited the stock's recent run higher and the vaccine maker's murky outlook for the call. He believes the commercialization of the Nuvaxovid Covid-19 shot could face obstacles to meaningful revenue growth.

In addition, "we expect the higher burden of proof and cost for pivotal trials under the new FDA framework may raise the bar for signing new partnerships for Novavax's COVID-19/influenza combination (CIC) vaccine program," he wrote in a note to clients.

The stock has gained nearly 9.5% so far this year.

_— Michelle Fox_

## JPMorgan Chase buying Apple Card from Goldman Sachs is a 'win win,' says Wells Fargo

People walk in front of a J.P. Morgan Financial Center in New York City, U.S., July 16, 2025.

Kylie Cooper \| Reuters

JPMorgan Chase purchasing the roughly $19 billion Apple credit card portfolio from Goldman Sachs could be a win for both firms, according to Wells Fargo.

"\[T\]here are a number of strategic and financial synergies from targeting personalized marketing efforts to a loyal customer base to layering a card portfolio on what is already one of the most efficient consumer banking platforms," analyst Mike Mayo wrote in a Tuesday note. "JPM would likely leverage its large consumer data set to enhance underwriting and improve personalized marketing and offers; this could be aided by Apple's and JPM's strong brand recognition and loyalty."

_— Brian Evans_

## Worry over economic conditions dominated July Fed meeting, minutes show

Federal Reserve officials signaled concern over inflation and the labor market at their July policy meeting while the majority still maintained that its too soon for a rate cut, according to [minutes released Wednesday](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/08/20/fed-minutes-august-2025.html).

"Participants generally pointed to risks to both sides of the Committee's dual mandate, emphasizing upside risk to inflation and downside risk to employment," the minutes said. While "a majority of participants judged the upside risk to inflation as the greater of these two risks" a couple saw "downside risk to employment the more salient risk."

## Palantir, Medtronic among stocks making biggest midday moves

_Here are some of the stocks posting the biggest moves in midday trading Wednesday._

- [Palantir Technologies](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/PLTR/)  — The defense technology company headed for a sixth consecutive losing day, dropping more than 2% on Wednesday. If Palantir closes in negative territory, that will mark its first six-day losing run since April 2024. Shares have more than doubled in 2025.
- [Medtronic](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/MDT/) — The medical device company saw shares pop 4% after giving guidance that was better than hoped. For the 2026 fiscal year, the company sees a tariff impact of about $185 million, down from its earlier range of roughly $200 million to $250 million. Medtronic also lifted its non-GAAP guidance for the year to a range of $5.60 to $5.66 per share, up from its earlier call for $5.50 to $5.60 per share and topping the FactSet consensus of $5.55 per share.
- [Avis Budget](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/CAR/) — Shares of the car rental company slipped 5%. Bank of America [downgraded Avis to underperform](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/08/20/wall-street-stocks-from-analyst-calls-like-nvidia.html) from buy. "We think that CAR fundamentals and the macro environment don't support the current stock price which significantly outperformed the market in June," the firm said.

## Dow's worst performers get a bump

The worst-performing stocks in the [Dow](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.DJI/) this year have recovered some losses in recent days.

[UnitedHealth](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/UNH/) shares have dropped more than 40% in 2025. But over the last five trading days, the stock has climbed more than 9%.

[Salesforce](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/CRM/) and [Merck](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/MRK/) have tumbled more than 26% and 14%, respectively. Both stocks have added more than 3% over the last five days.

## Tech stocks account for 40% of the market's biggest losers Wednesday and 5% of biggest winners

Only [Analog Devices](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/ADI/), up about 2.6%, lands in the top 20 percentage gains in the S&P 1500 index, comprised of the largecap S&P 500, midcap S&P 400 and smallcap S&P 600.

By contrast, about eight out of 20 of the market's largest losers consist of tech shares, led by [Palantir](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/PLTR/), down 7.3%, [Ichor Holdings](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/ICHR/), off by 7.1%, [Intel](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/INTC/), lower by 7%, [Micron Technology](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/MU/), down 5.8%, and [Dell Technologies](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/DELL/), off 4.9%.

Alex Karp, CEO of Palantir Technologies, speaks to the Economic Club of New York in New York City, U.S., February 24, 2025.

Palantir shares were down another 7% on Wednesday, the sixth consecutive session that the stock has fallen. The artificial intelligence software provider had hit all-time highs after reporting strong financial results earlier this month.

## Dan Ives: Tuesday's tech sell-off is nothing to fret about

Wall Street tech bull Dan Ives is looking at Tuesday's sell-off in technology stocks as an opportunity to own "core winners" in the artificial intelligence space.

"Skepticism will persist and on the sell-offs with some volatility the bears will come out of hibernation mode and try to spark more white knuckle moments ... this is a dynamic we have seen play out again and again since January 2023," Ives, Wedbush Securities global head of technology research, said in a [Wednesday morning post on X](https://x.com/DivesTech/status/1958119910745493703). "In our view the tech bull cycle will be well intact at least for another 2-3 years given the trillions being spent on AI infrastructure/software/chips/power/apps looking ahead. This remains our tech playbook and investor road map."

The tech-heavy [Nasdaq Composite](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.IXIC/) on Tuesday fell 1.46% to settle at 21,314.95. Shares of several megacap tech and semiconductor names, such as [Nvidia](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/NVDA/), [Advanced Micro Devices](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/AMD/) and [Palantir](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/PLTR/), declined during the session.

The partnership gives the car rental company more visibility and a potential profit boost for its car sales business.

Under the partnership, customers can browse from thousands of used Hertz vehicles on [Amazon Autos](https://www.cnbc.com/2023/11/16/amazon-to-let-dealers-sell-cars-on-its-site-starting-with-hyundai.html), e-sign the paperwork, complete their purchase online and pick up their vehicle at Hertz locations. ## Target falls on sales decline, CEO departure

[Target](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/TGT/) shares fell 8% after the company reported another quarter in which sales declined.

The retailer said comparable store sales fell 1.9% year over year. Consumer transactions also fell 1.3%, while the average amount consumers spent on those transactions slid by 0.6%.

On top of that, Target announced longtime CEO Brian Cornell would leave his post in February. Chief operating officer Michael Fiddelke, a 20-year veteran at the company, will become chief executive on Feb. 1.

## U.S. looks into taking equity stakes in chipmakers, report says

The Intel logo is displayed on a sign in front of Intel headquarters on July 16, 2025 in Santa Clara, California.

Justin Sullivan \| Getty Images

The U.S. is looking into taking equity stakes in Intel and other semiconductor makers in exchange for grants under the CHIPS Act, [Reuters reported, citing sources](https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/us-examines-equity-stake-chip-makers-chips-act-cash-grants-sources-say-2025-08-20/).

[Intel](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/INTC/) shares were down more than 1% in the premarket following the report, while [Micron Technology](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/MU/) shed 3%. The [VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH)](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/SMH/) lost 0.2%.

## Private equity stocks languish in August

President Donald Trump's move to grant savers [greater access to alternative assets](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/08/08/alternative-assets-head-for-your-401k-what-investors-need-to-know.html) in 401(k) plans hasn't been enough to spare private equity stocks from a rocky August.

[Blackstone](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/BX/), [KKR](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/KKR/), [Apollo](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/APO/) and [Ares Management](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/ARES/) are on pace to snap multi-month winning streaks. All four of the names are down between 2.7% and 5.7% in August, and they are also lagging the S&P 500 on a year-to-date basis.

## Longer-dated fixed-income yields at risk of rising, Capital Economics says

Long-dated government bonds of 10 years or more "have been under serious pressure at times this year," thanks to waning demand from traditional buyers, and "we doubt it's coming back," Capital Economics head of markets for Asia-Pacific Thomas Mathews wrote Tuesday.

The problem is that central banks themselves — as part of their move to normalize monetary policy and reduce their balance sheets — have stepped back from supporting the longer end of the market since the days of Quantitative Easing and zero interest rate policy.

"They'd provided a key source of demand for government bonds across the curve, and in many places held a very large share of the market. Demand has picked up from other sources to offset this reduction in demand from central banks. But, it hasn't mostly been from institutions that typically purchase very-long-dated government bonds," Mathews wrote.

"In the absence of genuine fiscal adjustment, which generally seems unlikely to us, we suspect that the very long end of the curve will remain volatile. And there's a good chance that yields rise ... again, at least for a while," Mathews added.
